title: Practice 5: Мне нравится, нужно, надо, можно

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: По какому бы это ___ (случай) было?..
exercises.why: The logical subject, that is the person who has to do something, is in the dative case: *Надо идти в класс.* The logical subject, when used with можно or нельзя, is in the dative case: *Вам можно курить, а мне нельзя. Отцу нельзя пить вино, а брату можно. The person who needs something (or someone) is in the dative case. The thing (or person) needed is in the nominative case, and the word нужен (-а, -о, -ы) agrees in gender and number with the thing (or person) needed: *Мне нужна книга. Нам нужны книги. To like — нравиться. This verb is used with the agent in the Dative case and the object (of the liking) in the Nominative case: *Мне нравится эта книга.* — I like this book. (Lit.: This book… — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lessons 35, 36, 41, 66.  ·  «The person who needs something (or someone) is in the dative case … The logical subject, when used with можно or нельзя, is in the dative case.» «This verb (нравиться) is used with the agent in the Dative case and the object (of the liking) in the Nominative case.» — DLI, Lessons 35, 36, 66.

Отцу нельзя пить вино, а брату можно. The person who needs something (or someone) is in the dative case. The thing (or person) needed is in the nominative case, and the word нужен (-а, -о, -ы) agrees in gender and number with the thing (or person) needed: *Мне нужна книга. Нам нужны книги. To like — нравиться. This verb is used with the agent in the Dative case and the object (of the liking) in the Nominative case: *Мне нравится эта книга.* — I like this book. (Lit.: This book… — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lessons 35, 36, 41, 66.  ·  «The person who needs something (or someone) is in the dative case … The logical subject, when used with можно or нельзя, is in the dative case.» «This verb (нравиться) is used with the agent in the Dative case and the object (of the liking) in the Nominative case.» — DLI, Lessons 35, 36, 66.
